antidotes.why: The epics first send someone to sit with the griever before any teaching.

antidotes.source: Ashma Gita; Valmiki 2.105; Narada to Shuka
antidotes.why: Understanding meets the mind's pain when meeting and parting come to all.
Feelings come and go, so bear them, because your wisdom is asleep, not gone.
Surrender is the Gita's last word, 'Do not grieve'.

chains.summary: Seeing his own people, Arjuna is overcome and his limbs fail. He drops the bow and sits down in grief. He cannot tell which course is better. Confused about what is right, he asks to be taught.
chains.title: Arjuna's collapse

verses.m: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥

verses.m: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verses.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥

verses.m: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥

chains.summary: Narada knows every science and says that he knows the words, not the self, and he grieves. Sanatkumara leads him inward. One speaks truth when one understands. One understands when one reflects. One reflects when one has trust. One has trust when one is steadfast. One is steadfast when one acts. One acts when one finds joy. Joy is in the vast, not in the small.
chains.title: Narada: learned and still grieving

verses.m: 'Sir, I know only the texts; I do not know the self. I have heard from people like you that one who knows the self crosses beyond sorrow. I am in sorrow, sir. Please take me across.' He said to him: 'Whatever you have studied is only name.'
verses.sa: सोऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविदेवास्मि नात्मविच्छ्रुतꣳ ह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्यस्तरति शोकमात्मविदिति सोऽहं भगवः शोचामि तं मा भगवाञ्छोकस्य पारं तारयत्विति तꣳ होवाच यद्वै किंचैतदध्यगीष्ठा नामैवैतत् ॥

verses.m: When one acts, one becomes steadfast. One does not become steadfast without acting; only by acting does one become steadfast. So action itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand action.'
verses.sa: यदा वै करोत्यथ निस्तिष्ठति नाकृत्वा निस्तिष्ठति कृत्वैव निस्तिष्ठति कृतिस्त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्येति कृतिं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥

verses.m: When one finds happiness, one acts. No one acts without finding happiness; only by finding happiness does one act. So happiness itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand happiness.'
verses.sa: यदा वै सुखं लभतेऽथ करोति नासुखं लब्ध्वा करोति सुखमेव लब्ध्वा करोति सुखं त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यमिति सुखं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥

chains.summary: Dwelling on what is lost adds a second sorrow to the first. The medicine for sorrow is not to keep thinking of it. Thought about, sorrow does not leave, it grows. Meet the mind's pain with understanding and the body's with medicine.
chains.title: Not dwelling on it is the medicine

verses.m: When pain of body or mind arrives and nothing can be done about it, do not keep thinking about it. Not dwelling on it is the medicine for sorrow; brooding does not make it leave, it only makes it grow.
verses.sa: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् / चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते / यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्

verses.m: Heal the pain of the mind with wisdom and the pain of the body with medicine. That is what knowledge can do; don't behave like a child about it.
verses.sa: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः / एतद्विज्ञानमसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात्

verses.m: No one should sit alone grieving over a trouble that has struck everyone. Instead of grieving, act to remedy it if you see a way.
verses.sa: न जानपदिकं दुःखमेकः शोचितुमर्हति / अशोचन्प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम्

chains.summary: Pain of the mind comes from two places: the mind's own confusion, or something unwanted happening. There is no third. In grief, ask where I came from, where I am going, and who I am.
chains.title: Two sources of the mind's pain

verses.m: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verses.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.sa: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते

verses.m: 'Where was I before? Where will I go? Who am I, really, and why am I here? Why should I grieve, and for what?' Ask these, and steady the mind.
verses.r: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verses.sa: क्वासे क्व च गमिष्यामि कोऽन्वहं किमिहास्थितः / कस्मात्किमनुशोचेयमित्येवं स्थापयेन्मनः

depicts.m: From happiness you have fallen into sorrow; you will come to happiness again. No one has sorrow forever, and no one has happiness forever.
depicts.sa: सुखात्त्वं दुःखमापन्नः पुनरापत्स्यसे सुखम् / न नित्यं लभते दुःखं न नित्यं लभते सुखम्
depicts.why: Depicts a father addressed as one fallen from happiness into sorrow.

depicts.m: There is no shade like a mother, no refuge like a mother, no protection like a mother, no one as dear as a mother.
depicts.sa: नास्ति मातृसमा च्छाया नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः / नास्ति मातृसमं त्राणं नास्ति मातृसमा प्रिया
depicts.why: Shows the size of the loss for one who has lost her.

depicts.m: Friend, I am mad with love, and no one knows my pain. Only the wounded know what the wounded go through, only one who has been wounded.
depicts.r: Meera pada "Mero darad na jane koy"
depicts.sa: हे री मैं तो प्रेम-दिवानी मेरो दरद न जाणै कोय। घायल की गति घायल जाणै, जो कोई घायल होय।

depicts.m: He was known as supremely detached, yet on seeing Sita his composure fled. The king held Janaki to his heart, and the great banks of his wisdom gave way.
depicts.sa: सीय बिलोकि धीरता भागी। रहे कहावत परम बिरागी॥ लीन्हि रायँ उर लाइ जानकी। मिटी महामरजाद ग्यान की ॥
depicts.why: Shows a father famed for calm losing his composure at the parting.

depicts.m: You give me simple advice, the kind that would do me good if I followed it. Though I understand it well, my heart is not at peace.
depicts.sa: तुम्ह तौ देहु सरल सिख सोई। जो आचरत मोर भल होई॥ जद्यपि यह समुझत हउँ नीकें। तदपि होत परितोष न जी कें ॥
depicts.why: Shows understanding does not reach the grief.

depicts.m: Thinking this over, I will not insist out of false affection. I bless you, son; only keep the bond of a mother, and don't forget me.
depicts.sa: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥
depicts.why: Shows she lets him go and can ask only not to be forgotten.

depicts.m: Stay well, mother Yashoda. In four or five days we two brothers will come. Since the day I was parted from you, no one has called me "Kanhaiya". I have not had breakfast in the morning, nor warm milk at evening.
depicts.sa: नीके रहियो जसुमति मैया। आवैंगे दिन चारि पाँच में हम हलधर दोउ भैया॥ जा दिन तें हम तुमतें बिछुरे काहु न कह्यो 'कन्हैया'। कबहूँ प्रात न कियो कलेवा, साँझ न पीन्हीं धैया॥
depicts.why: Shows the small daily cares of a mother are gone.

depicts.m: Night and day our eyes keep raining. Ever since Shyam went away, it is always the rainy season for us.
depicts.sa: निसिदिन बरसत नैन हमारे। सदा रहति पावस ऋतु हम पै जब तें स्याम सिधारे॥

gloss: Śoka is the burning of loss. Arjuna says it dries up his senses (2.8), and Narada says he knows the mantras and still grieves (Chandogya 7.1.3).

heals.m: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
heals.why: Places pain among things that come and go.

heals.m: My child, bless you, hold on to courage even now. Seeing that the times are bad, set aside your grief. Knowing that the course of time and karma cannot be turned, don't take this loss as your shame.
heals.sa: अजहुँ बच्छ बलि धीरज धरहू। कुसमउ समुझि सोक परिहरहू॥ जनि मानहु हियँ हानि गलानी। काल करम गति अघटित जानी ॥
heals.why: A grieving mother asks him to hold on, so he is not alone in it.

heals.m: 'Sir, I know only the texts; I do not know the self. I have heard from people like you that one who knows the self crosses beyond sorrow. I am in sorrow, sir. Please take me across.' He said to him: 'Whatever you have studied is only name.'
heals.sa: सोऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविदेवास्मि नात्मविच्छ्रुतꣳ ह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्यस्तरति शोकमात्मविदिति सोऽहं भगवः शोचामि तं मा भगवाञ्छोकस्य पारं तारयत्विति तꣳ होवाच यद्वै किंचैतदध्यगीष्ठा नामैवैतत् ॥

heals.m: Your understanding, wise one, is beyond even the gods' reckoning. Grief has only put your wisdom to sleep, and I am here to wake it.
heals.sa: बुद्धिश्च ते महाप्राज्ञ देवैरपि दुरन्वया। शोकेनाभिप्रसुप्तं ते ज्ञानं सम्बोधयाम्यहम्॥
heals.why: Treats grief as a sleep over wisdom, not its loss.

heals.m: Take heart, best of men. Which living being does trouble not touch? Troubles strike like fire, king, and pass in a moment.
heals.sa: आश्वसिही नरश्रेष्ठ प्राणिनः कस्य नापदः। संस्पृशन्त्यग्निवद् राजन् क्षणेन व्यपयान्ति च॥
heals.why: Shows sorrow common to all, not a mark against him.

heals.m: I am the goal, the sustainer, the master, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend; the origin and the dissolution, the ground, the treasure-house and the undying seed.
heals.sa: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
heals.why: Shows the one who holds origin and ending as witness and refuge.

heals.m: What was, ceases to be; what was not, comes to be. Grief has no power to change this. Why then should anyone grieve?
heals.sa: भूत्वा च न भवत्येतदभूत्वा च भविष्यति / शोके न ह्यस्ति सामर्थ्यं शोचेत स कथं नरः
heals.why: Shows grief having no power over what has already changed, freeing the energy it was holding.

heals.m: From happiness you have fallen into sorrow; you will come to happiness again. No one has sorrow forever, and no one has happiness forever.
heals.sa: सुखात्त्वं दुःखमापन्नः पुनरापत्स्यसे सुखम् / न नित्यं लभते दुःखं न नित्यं लभते सुखम्
heals.why: Shows sorrow placed in a turning cycle, with return promised.

hero.m: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
hero.sa: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥

loci.m: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
loci.sa: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥

loci.m: Knowing the self as bodiless within bodies, steady among the unsteady, great and all-pervading, the wise one does not grieve.
loci.sa: अशरीरँ शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् । महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥

practices.m: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
practices.why: Bearing what passes without being moved.

practices.m: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on every side, a person withdraws the senses from their objects, his wisdom is firmly set.
practices.sa: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
practices.why: Shows wisdom staying set when the senses are gathered.

practices.m: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
practices.sa: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
practices.why: Cultivates the capacity to hold steady while the surge passes.

practices.m: Whether a task is good or bad, a wise person should first carefully weigh its outcome. The result of deeds done in great haste burns the heart like a thorn until one's dying day.
practices.sa: गुणवदगुणवद्वा कुर्वता कार्यजातं परिणतिरवधार्या यत्नतः पण्डितेन । अतिरभसकृतानां कर्मणामाविपत्ते- र्भवति हृदयदाही शल्यतुल्यो विपाकः ॥

practices.m: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
practices.sa: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥
practices.why: Shows removal of dullness of mind.

practices.m: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
practices.sa: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥

practices.m: Make a friend slowly, and give one up slowly. A friendship made slowly is one that lasts long.
practices.sa: चिरेण मित्रं बध्नीयाच्चिरेण च कृतं त्यजेत् / चिरेण हि कृतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति
practices.why: Take time before binding or breaking a bond.

practices.m: Do not wound others where it hurts, do not speak cruelly, do not take from those who have less. Never say words that make another person flinch; such words are scorching and lead to dark places.
practices.sa: नारुतुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी / न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत / ययाऽस्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत / न तां वदेदुशतिं पापलोक्याम्
practices.why: Shows one feeling the other's flinch before speaking.

stories.l: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
stories.s: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango tree. Even when he went astray, he was taken back.
stories.t: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps

stories.l: Loyalty means staying through the bad season, not only the good.
stories.s: A hunter's poisoned arrow withers the tree where a parrot has always lived. The parrot refuses to leave it. Indra, moved by its loyalty, restores the tree.
stories.t: The parrot who stayed with the withered tree

stories.l: The hardest battle is with your own mind, and no one else can fight it for you.
stories.s: As Yudhishthira still grieves, Krishna tells him his real battle has begun: one fought alone, with his own mind, where 'mine' is death and 'not mine' is freedom.

stories.l: You can live amid plenty without being owned by it.
stories.s: Bharat places Ram's sandals on the throne and lives outside the city in a hut, sleeping on grass, fasting, governing only as a caretaker. The palace's riches are all around him and do not touch him, like a bee in a champak garden.
stories.t: Bharat rules from a hut for fourteen years
